title: Modeling coal-ash chemistry as a multi-output problem
summary: I developed multi-output XGBoost research workflows to estimate related coal-ash constituents from shared predictors. The work progressed from separate oxide estimators to a shared-tree experiment with compositional transformation, group-aware splitting and constituent-level diagnostics, addressing how chemical targets should be modeled and evaluated together.
role: Data scientist · Feature engineering, multi-output modeling and evaluation
context: Leidos research supporting DOE/NETL · Coal-ash characterization

problem: Coal ash varies in chemical composition, and related oxide percentages are not independent targets. A useful predictive workflow needs to account for multiple constituents, related samples and the interpretation of percentage-based outputs while preserving laboratory measurements as the reference.
contribution: I explored two multi-target XGBoost approaches: separate estimators wrapped in MultiOutputRegressor, followed by a shared-tree multi-output experiment. The documented full analysis combines oxide preprocessing, engineered predictors, compositional transformation, grouped model selection and diagnostics in both transformed and percentage space.

approach.title: Define the chemistry targets
approach.body: Modeled ten oxide percentages: SiO₂, Al₂O₃, Fe₂O₃, CaO, MgO, Na₂O, K₂O, TiO₂, P₂O₅ and SO₃. Predictors included mine type, energy type, coal-mine state and selected fractional and Jin_ variables.

approach.title: Prepare values for compositional analysis
approach.body: Represented below-detection measurements by half the reported limit and replaced nonpositive values with a small positive constant for log-ratio calculations. Training-data medians supplied missing target values before transformation.

approach.title: Progress from separate estimators to shared structure
approach.body: The initial workflow fitted separate XGBoost estimators per oxide. The later experiment used shared tree structure with vector-valued outputs and a centered log-ratio transformation based on the components’ geometric mean.

approach.title: Respect sample grouping during evaluation
approach.body: Used a group-aware 70/30 split based on Plant_Name_State_Year and five-fold GroupKFold for Bayesian tuning. A separate grouped validation subset supported early stopping. The weighted MAE objective emphasized selected lower-concentration constituents, including SO₃, Na₂O and P₂O₅.

approach.title: Evaluate in the units that matter
approach.body: Calculated per-oxide MAE, RMSE and R² in transformed space, then inverse-transformed predictions to normalized percentages. Diagnostics included Aitchison distance, compositional closure, weighted percentage error and mean absolute log error.

outcome: The result is a documented research workflow for comparing multi-output strategies and examining errors by chemical constituent. It provides a basis for investigating material composition and model suitability. No unverified numerical performance claims are added to this case study, and the research implementation and data remain private.
learning: The progression from independent target models to shared-tree compositional modeling demonstrates how a familiar algorithm can be adapted to a new scientific constraint. The work also connects model selection to data structure: related samples need grouped evaluation, while percentage outputs require an explicit definition of the compositional whole.
limitations: Predicted chemistry requires confirmation against laboratory measurements; it does not establish recovery economics or material suitability.
The implementation and source data are private, so this public case study presents the method rather than a reproducible benchmark.
Target imputation inside cross-validation folds remains a methodological review item.
The inverse transformation closes the ten modeled components to 100%. That normalization must match the intended compositional whole before percentage predictions are interpreted.

evidence.title: Two documented modeling strategies
evidence.body: The initial and later approaches are distinct research configurations. The comparison below describes their design, not a claim that one achieved better independent performance.

rows: Shared-tree multi-output XGBoost with vector-valued predictions

evidence.title: Evaluation design
evidence.body: The full analysis documents grouped splitting by plant, state and year, grouped cross-validation, a validation subset for early stopping, and per-constituent error assessment. Missing-value treatment and the chosen compositional closure remain explicit review items.
